chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Everything in which there is both the permissible and the prohibited, it is permissible for you forever until you recognize the prohibited from it specifically, so you should leave it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on food or items where we are unsure if they contain haram elements?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the foundational juristic principle of 'istishab al-halal' (presumption of permissibility), asserting that mixed items remain lawful until the specific prohibited component is distinctly identified. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on certainty over doubt, requiring active identification of the haram element rather than assuming impurity by default. This ruling facilitates daily ease for believers by maintaining the status quo of permissibility in ambiguous situations.
